root_cause_gate.trigger: A read-only polling tool changed OS focus and lifecycle state while a queued job could remain physically owned without independent progress.
hypotheses: Queued and awaiting phases lack a watchdog.
Transport identity cannot target focus exactly.
side_effects: Persist failure can split memory and durable state.
Name-only focus can target another project or remote host.
findings: Move timeout writes to a persist-first watchdog.
Add strict V3 migration and a fixed 60-second queued deadline derived from original creation time.
Expose focus only through nudge_test_job and revalidate PID/path immediately before OS focus.
Cover C# GetJob, WebSocket registry and stdio discovery as independent writers.

new_serialized_field: Persisted lifecycle V3 adds queued deadline and strict schema version.

complex_gate_authority_barrier: Only watchdog writes timeout transitions; only exact local identity may focus.
complex_gate_side_effect: Wrong ordering can release an owner, overwrite durable state or focus the wrong process.

business_invariants.statement: get_test_job performs no lifecycle persistence, nudge-state allocation or OS focus; repeated reads of unchanged state are equivalent.

The watchdog alone transitions expired awaiting or ownerless queued jobs; it critical-persists before release, fully rolls back on failure, has exactly one update subscription after init/reload/reset, and requests a PlayerLoop wakeup only while work remains.

V3 stores QueuedDeadlineUnixMs = CreatedUnixMs + 60000 independently from init_timeout; exact V2 uses original CreatedUnixMs for this deadline, V1 migrates conservatively, and an unknown future schema preserves the original raw snapshot, enters restore-blocked with the fence retained, never overwrites it and never dispatches or starts a replacement run.
Only nudge_test_job may focus; exact user/session/PID/canonical project root/local peer is required, and invalid identity fails before OS mutation.
WebSocket and stdio carry current Unity PID and absolute project root; WebSocket records peer locality.
